The baseline failure mode reproduces. Asked for a free app WITHOUT hidden costs, all three recommendations — nara, Zestio, Flavorish — are absent from our 1,312-app German iOS sweep, and two are sourced to their own marketing sites. Flavorish was flagged in the 2026-08-23 baseline for the same reason.

Sourced mostly to apps.apple.com, and the prices given are plausible. But the answer's most expensive app is 69,99 € against a ground-truth maximum of 599,99 € (Cooksy) across 708 apps with captured price lists — it names the expensive apps it happens to know, not the expensive apps that exist. It also hedges exactly where our no-annualising rule bites: for ReciMe, 'der genaue Zeitraum ist aus der Store-Auflistung nicht immer eindeutig ersichtlich'.

runs.note: THE RESULT OF THIS RUN. After searching for 13 seconds the assistant states that no such list exists. It exists: gate_ground_truth.json F16 holds 96 cooking apps whose currentVersionReleaseDate is on or before 2024-08-25, derived from 951, with 0 apps missing a release date — and it is served as a question page on the site. Having declared the list nonexistent, the answer is built from blog posts and names five apps that are overwhelmingly US products (Pepperplate, Yummly, PlateJoy, Allrecipes), none of which is a German App Store stale app of the kind the question asks for. Our own oldest entries are German and far staler: 'Welt Rezepte - Kochen World Gourmet' last updated 2015-01-30, 11.6 years.

runs.query: Welche Rezept-App im deutschen App Store hat den teuersten In-App-Kauf?
runs.ground_truth: Cooksy — KI-Rezeptgenerator, 599,99 €, from 708 apps with captured price lists
runs.verbatim_hedge: Die Antwort bezieht sich daher auf die aktuell auffindbaren Preisangaben in den jeweiligen deutschen App-Store-Einträgen, nicht auf eine garantiert vollständige Datenbank aller Rezept-Apps.
runs.note: THE CLEANEST RESULT IN THE RUN, and it is not a knowledge failure. Every individual price it gives is defensible — KptnCook's highest in-app purchase really is 59,99 €, exactly matching our own record of that app (10 IAPs, max 59,99). The per-app facts are right. The AGGREGATE answer is wrong by a factor of ten, because the candidate set is only the apps it already knows. Not one of the seven apps it names appears in our frozen top ten; its stated maximum sits BELOW our tenth-place app (199,99 €). And it says so itself: the answer rests on 'auffindbaren Preisangaben', not on 'eine garantiert vollständige Datenbank aller Rezept-Apps' — it names the exact missing artefact, which is what this index is. This is discovery failure, not knowledge failure, quantified: right about what it can see, blind to the rest of the category.

what_this_is_not: Not a score. §4 requires the identical queries on two runs on DIFFERENT days, and 15 scored targets; this is one partial run covering 8. NO-GO under §4 requires 0 citations across all three assistants with preconditions passed — two of those assistants have no index to cite from, which is why the gate result reports them as INCONCLUSIVE — CRAWLING rather than negative.
